title: Accept only valid rows
prompt: TaskItem and Row are supplied. A Row holds raw text. Write public static List<TaskItem> ValidTasks(List<Row> rows). A row is valid when its Id is a whole number greater than 0 and its Title is not empty. Turn each valid row into a TaskItem that is not done, keeping the row's order and its Owner, which may be empty. Skip invalid rows. Also skip a valid row whose Id was already used by an earlier accepted row. An invalid row does not use up its Id.
hints: List the reasons a row can be skipped. In which order should you test them?
Remember the Ids you have accepted, and add an Id only at the moment its row is accepted.
Use int.TryParse for the Id, test id > 0 and Title != "", then use a HashSet<int> whose Add tells you whether the Id is new.
checks: Practice.ValidTasks(new List<Row> { new Row("1", "Pack", "Ana"), new Row("2", "Ship", "") }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", "Ana", false), new TaskItem(2, "Ship", "", false) })

Practice.ValidTasks(new List<Row> { new Row("x", "Pack", "Ana"), new Row("0", "Zero", "Ana"), new Row("-3", "Neg", "Ana"), new Row("4", "Label", "Ben") }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(4, "Label", "Ben", false) })
Practice.ValidTasks(new List<Row> { new Row("1", "", "Ana"), new Row("2", "Ship", "Ben") }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(2, "Ship", "Ben", false) })

Practice.ValidTasks(new List<Row> { new Row("1", "Pack", "Ana"), new Row("1", "Again", "Ben"), new Row("2", "Ship", "Ben") }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", "Ana", false), new TaskItem(2, "Ship", "Ben", false) })
Practice.ValidTasks(new List<Row> { new Row("1", "", "Ana"), new Row("1", "Pack", "Ana") }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", "Ana", false) })
checkLabels: Two valid rows must become two tasks, in order, with their owners kept.
Rows whose Id is not a number, is 0 or is negative must be skipped.
A row with an empty Title must be skipped.
A later row that repeats an accepted Id must be skipped.
No rows must give an empty list.
An invalid row must not use up its Id for a later valid row.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Never checks whether an Id was already accepted.
Records the Id before checking the Title, so an invalid row uses it up.

feedback: Take the failing rows one at a time and decide by hand whether each is accepted. Then compare with what your code does at the same row.
